system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Tokyo, Japan. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Tokyo itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Tokyo space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Roppongi, Ginza/Kyobashi, Nihonbashi/Bakurocho, Shibuya/Omotesando, Shinjuku/Kagurazaka, Ebisu/Meguro, Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, Tennozu, Ueno/Yanaka, Setagaya/West Tokyo) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Tokyo spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Tokyo, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: SCAI THE BATHHOUSE
galleries.note: Converted 200-year-old bathhouse; since 1993 the key bridge between Japanese postwar masters (Kusama, Lee Ufan, Miyajima) and the international scene.

galleries.name: Taka Ishii Gallery
galleries.note: Global-facing programme in photography and contemporary art, with Maebashi/NY/LA history and a heavy fair presence; anchor of the complex665 building.

galleries.name: Ota Fine Arts
galleries.note: Yayoi Kusama's long-time Tokyo dealer, with Singapore and Shanghai outposts and a strong pan-Asian conceptual roster.

galleries.name: ShugoArts
galleries.note: Rigorous programme of Japanese artists (Yasumasa Morimura, Tomoko Yoneda, Shimabuku) with consistent museum placements.

galleries.name: Tomio Koyama Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 1996; helped launch Nara, Murakami and Kusama internationally and remains one of Tokyo's most fair-active dealers.

galleries.name: Take Ninagawa
galleries.note: Critically respected programme linking Mono-ha and Gutai legacies to younger international artists; regular at Art Basel and Frieze.

galleries.name: Mizuma Art Gallery
galleries.note: Since 1994 the platform for Aida Makoto, Yamaguchi Akira and 'Neo-Nihonga'; strong Asian network with Singapore and Beijing ties.

galleries.name: Perrotin Tokyo
galleries.note: Tokyo branch of the French mega-gallery; high-profile shows of Murakami, JR, Sophie Calle and Japanese debuts of blue-chip names.

galleries.name: Pace Gallery Tokyo
galleries.note: Pace's permanent Tokyo space (2024) in Azabudai Hills, bringing international blue-chip programming to central Tokyo.

galleries.name: Gagosian Tokyo
galleries.note: Longest-standing international mega-gallery outpost in Tokyo, presenting museum-grade shows of its global roster.

galleries.name: BLUM
galleries.note: The LA gallery's Tokyo space; historically decisive for Superflat and for reintroducing postwar Japanese art to the West.

galleries.name: Kaikai Kiki Gallery
galleries.note: Takashi Murakami's gallery arm, incubator for a generation of younger Japanese artists and a global-facing brand.

galleries.name: Tokyo Gallery + BTAP
galleries.note: Japan's first contemporary gallery (1950); historic for Mono-ha and for opening Beijing's 798 with BTAP.

galleries.name: Gallery Koyanagi
galleries.note: Elegant Ginza mainstay showing Sugimoto, Rinko Kawauchi, Olafur Eliasson and other international names since 1995.

galleries.name: NANZUKA UNDERGROUND
galleries.note: Defined the pop/illustration-to-fine-art crossover (Hajime Sorayama, Keiichi Tanaami, Haroshi); multiple Tokyo venues and heavy fair presence.

galleries.name: Taro Nasu
galleries.note: Conceptually driven programme (Ryan Gander, Simon Fujiwara, Koki Tanaka) with strong European connections.

galleries.name: Misako & Rosen
galleries.note: Small but internationally influential; a fixture of Basel/Liste-type discourse and a model for artist-led curatorial exchange.

galleries.name: Yutaka Kikutake Gallery
galleries.note: Sharp younger-generation programme; consistent presence at Art Basel Hong Kong and Frieze.

galleries.name: KOSAKU KANECHIKA
galleries.note: Museum-quality installations by Mika Ninagawa, Yuko Mohri and Sanya Kantarovsky; a driver of Tennozu's rise.

galleries.name: ANOMALY
galleries.note: Large-scale space formed by the merger of three veteran dealers; ambitious shows of Chim↑Pom, Ei Arakawa and others.

galleries.name: KOTARO NUKAGA
galleries.note: Fast-rising gallery with Tennozu and Roppongi spaces, mixing international emerging names with Japanese mid-career artists.

galleries.name: Maho Kubota Gallery
galleries.note: Thoughtful programme (Yuki Onodera, Kenji Yanobe collaborations, international photography) with growing fair visibility.

galleries.name: Fergus McCaffrey Tokyo
galleries.note: New York gallery's Tokyo space; scholarly presentations of Gutai and postwar Japanese avant-garde alongside Western artists.

galleries.name: MAKI Gallery
galleries.note: Multiple Tokyo spaces bringing internationally trending painters to Japan and supporting Japanese artists abroad.

galleries.name: Shiseido Gallery
galleries.note: Corporate gallery operating since 1919 — Japan's oldest continuously running exhibition space, with a genuinely experimental free programme.

galleries.name: Yumiko Chiba Associates
galleries.note: Custodian of key postwar photography and conceptual estates (Kishin Shinoyama, Ei-Q) plus contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Aoyama Meguro
galleries.note: Curatorially austere space run by Naoya Aoyama; a critics' favourite for conceptual and post-Mono-ha positions.

galleries.name: Kayokoyuki
galleries.note: Influential young gallery in the Komagome cluster, exporting emerging Japanese painters to Liste and Art Basel.

galleries.name: Misa Shin Gallery
galleries.note: Handles the Nobuo Sekine and On Kawara-adjacent legacies and politically engaged international artists; strong institutional ties.

galleries.name: Ginza Maison Hermès Le Forum
galleries.note: Free corporate kunsthalle with an internationally respected curatorial programme in Renzo Piano's glass-block tower.

galleries.name: Whitestone Gallery
galleries.note: Large commercial operation with Hong Kong, Taipei, Singapore and Seoul branches; major secondary market in Gutai and postwar Japan.

galleries.name: Kenji Taki Gallery
galleries.note: Nagoya-rooted gallery whose Tokyo space shows rigorous abstraction and European conceptualists; long track record.

galleries.name: Art Front Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 1970s; organiser behind the Echigo-Tsumari and Setouchi triennales, uniquely influential on Japan's art-festival model.

galleries.name: MEM
galleries.note: Scholarly programme rediscovering Japanese photography and outsider/queer histories (Toshio Matsumoto, Nobuyoshi Araki archives).

galleries.name: XYZ collective
galleries.note: Artist-run space that became a node in the international young-gallery network; launched many careers now shown worldwide.

galleries.name: PARCEL
galleries.note: Design-conscious space that made Bakurocho a destination; agile programme of emerging Japanese and overseas artists.

galleries.name: WAITINGROOM
galleries.note: Young gallery with an incisive eye for emerging artists and a growing presence at Asian fairs.

galleries.name: KEN NAKAHASHI
galleries.note: Shinjuku gallery known for queer, performance and body-based practices, including Genesis P-Orridge and Tetsumi Kudo-adjacent lineages.

galleries.name: Hagiwara Projects
galleries.note: Lean, artist-focused programme of contemporary painting and sculpture; a regular at Liste and Asian fairs.

galleries.name: MUJIN-TO Production
galleries.note: Politically engaged gallery, home of Chim↑Pom-era activism and post-3.11 art; punches far above its size critically.

galleries.name: Satoko Oe Contemporary
galleries.note: Curator-run gallery with a quiet, research-based programme and consistent international fair participation.

galleries.name: Kana Kawanishi Gallery
galleries.note: Photography and new-media focused; active in international exchange and prize-winning young artists.

galleries.name: URANO
galleries.note: Successor to ARATANIURANO; conceptual and media-art programme with long-standing critical credibility.

galleries.name: Yuka Tsuruno Gallery
galleries.note: Photography-leaning contemporary programme; among the first movers into the Tennozu art district.

galleries.name: Kodama Gallery
galleries.note: Kansai-founded gallery with a long record in conceptual and sculptural practices, now anchored in Tokyo.

galleries.name: Zen Foto Gallery
galleries.note: Specialist in Japanese and Chinese photography with a serious publishing arm; key to the international photobook scene.

galleries.name: PGI
galleries.note: Photo Gallery International, founded 1979 — Japan's pioneering fine-art photography dealer and print workshop.

galleries.name: AKIO NAGASAWA Gallery
galleries.note: Publisher-gallerist central to Daido Moriyama and Nobuyoshi Araki's global market; multiple Ginza spaces.

galleries.name: THE CLUB
galleries.note: Curatorially ambitious Ginza Six gallery pairing international contemporary names with Japanese historical material.

galleries.name: Nichido Contemporary Art
galleries.note: Contemporary arm of the venerable Galerie Nichido; consistent programme of mid-career Japanese and Asian artists.

galleries.name: Gallery MoMo
galleries.note: Two-venue gallery supporting figurative painting and sculpture by emerging and mid-career Japanese artists since 2004.
Artist-run space with an international exchange model; a key node for Tokyo's youngest experimental scene.

galleries.name: The 5th Floor
galleries.note: Curator-run experimental venue and residency-linked platform for the post-2020 generation of Tokyo artists.

galleries.name: WHITEHOUSE
galleries.note: Revived 1950s avant-garde building run by the Chim↑Pom circle; a hub for performance and countercultural programming.

galleries.name: Tokyo Arts and Space (TOKAS) Hongo
galleries.note: City-funded institution (formerly Tokyo Wonder Site) whose exhibitions and residencies have launched many careers.

galleries.name: gallery αM
galleries.note: Musashino Art University's free experimental space; annual guest-curated series are closely watched by critics.

galleries.name: Art Center Ongoing
galleries.note: Artist-run centre, cafe and archive in Kichijoji; a long-running incubator for Tokyo's alternative scene.

galleries.name: Youkobo Art Space
galleries.note: Pioneering micro-residency and gallery, connecting Tokyo to international residency networks for over two decades.

galleries.name: Arts Initiative Tokyo (AIT)
galleries.note: Curatorial nonprofit running residencies, the MAD education programme and exhibitions since 2001.

galleries.name: Spiral / Spiral Garden
galleries.note: Fumihiko Maki-designed cultural complex whose atrium and gallery have hosted landmark art and design shows since 1985.

galleries.name: Espace Louis Vuitton Tokyo
galleries.note: Free foundation space showing Fondation Louis Vuitton collection works and commissions in Omotesando.

galleries.name: Ginza Graphic Gallery (ggg)
galleries.note: DNP's graphic-design gallery since 1986; internationally the most important venue for Japanese design exhibitions.

galleries.name: POLA Museum Annex
galleries.note: Free corporate space in Ginza with a well-regarded programme of emerging and mid-career Japanese artists.

galleries.name: Chanel Nexus Hall
galleries.note: Corporate cultural hall known for photography exhibitions and cross-disciplinary programming.

galleries.name: Taguchi Fine Art
galleries.note: Long-running dealer of drawing, print and conceptual work with an idiosyncratic international roster.

galleries.name: Koki Arts
galleries.note: Photography-centred gallery in the Bakurocho cluster, active in international photo fairs.

galleries.name: Roentgenwerke AG
galleries.note: Descendant of the legendary 1990s Roentgen Kunst Institut that first showed Murakami and Nara.

galleries.name: Ando Gallery
galleries.note: Veteran dealer in minimal and conceptual art, publishing editions with Japanese and European artists since the 1980s.

galleries.name: Base Gallery
galleries.note: Long-established gallery showing painting and sculpture by mid-career Japanese artists.

galleries.name: √K Contemporary
galleries.note: Three-storey space combining contemporary shows with postwar Japanese art scholarship and publishing.

galleries.name: eitoeiko
galleries.note: Small Kagurazaka gallery with a socially and politically engaged programme and strong Asian exchange.

galleries.name: TALION GALLERY
galleries.note: Quiet, conceptually focused gallery respected for tightly argued solo exhibitions.

galleries.name: EUKARYOTE
galleries.note: Three-floor Jingumae space presenting a young, cross-genre roster with strong exhibition design.

galleries.name: The Mass
galleries.note: Harajuku venue bridging street/pop culture and contemporary art with frequent international collaborations.

galleries.name: Gallery Common
galleries.note: Compact Jingumae gallery with a sharp eye for young painters and illustration-adjacent practices.

galleries.name: VOILLD
galleries.note: Programme spanning contemporary art, craft and design culture; influential among younger collectors.

galleries.name: CALM & PUNK GALLERY
galleries.note: Long-running space at the intersection of art, music and street culture, with strong international guest shows.

galleries.name: POETIC SCAPE
galleries.note: Photography gallery with a distinctive editorial sensibility and a steady stream of first solo shows.

galleries.name: G/P gallery
galleries.note: Contemporary photography specialist that helped define the post-2000 Japanese photo scene.

galleries.name: Nishimura Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 1964; brought Hockney, Kitaj and British art to Japan and represents senior Japanese painters.

galleries.name: Shirota Gallery
galleries.note: Historic Ginza gallery (est. 1966) central to Japanese printmaking and to Yoko Ono/Fluxus-era exhibitions.

galleries.name: Galerie Tokyo Humanité
galleries.note: Kyobashi gallery of long standing with a serious abstraction and print programme plus an annex for younger artists.

galleries.name: Megumi Ogita Gallery
galleries.note: Known for launching young Japanese artists via its Odyssey competition and for consistent fair participation.

galleries.name: Gallery Tsubaki
galleries.note: Operating since 1974 with an annex space; a durable supporter of contemporary Japanese painting.

galleries.name: SEIZAN Gallery
galleries.note: Tokyo–New York gallery promoting Japanese artists internationally with a contemporary-meets-tradition programme.

galleries.name: Shibunkaku Tokyo
galleries.note: Kyoto house founded 1937; its Tokyo space stages scholarly shows linking classical Japanese art with contemporary practice.

galleries.name: A Lighthouse called Kanata
galleries.note: Gallery pairing contemporary art with Japanese antiquities and craft, with an international collector base.

galleries.name: SNOW Contemporary
galleries.note: Curator-founded gallery known for conceptual and socially engaged Japanese artists and off-site projects.

galleries.name: Kanda & Oliveira
galleries.note: Japanese–Brazilian gallery bringing Latin American and diaspora practices into the Tokyo conversation.

galleries.name: Gallery 360°
galleries.note: Fluxus and multiples specialist since 1981; an archive-like resource for conceptual editions and artists' books.

galleries.name: Yukiko Koide Presents
galleries.note: Leading Japanese venue for art brut and outsider art, with strong international exhibition partnerships.

galleries.name: Hidari Zingaro
galleries.note: Murakami-founded Nakano Broadway venue that turned otaku-adjacent subculture into a serious exhibition platform.

galleries.name: Komagome SOKO
galleries.note: Warehouse project space anchoring the Komagome cluster; large-scale installations by emerging artists.

galleries.name: TAV GALLERY
galleries.note: West Tokyo gallery with a distinctive, criticism-driven programme for the youngest generation.

galleries.name: void+
galleries.note: Compact Aoyama project space with a consistently experimental, non-commercial curatorial line.

galleries.name: CADAN Yurakucho
galleries.note: Shared exhibition space of the Contemporary Art Dealers Association of Nippon; a rotating window on the whole gallery scene.

galleries.name: OIL by Bijutsutecho Gallery
galleries.note: Gallery arm of Japan's leading art magazine; accessible programming that reaches a wide public audience.

galleries.name: HARMAS GALLERY
galleries.note: Small Nakameguro gallery with a considered programme of emerging painters and sculptors.

galleries.name: MASATAKA CONTEMPORARY
galleries.note: East Tokyo gallery supporting mid-career and emerging artists, part of the Sumida/Ryogoku art cluster.

galleries.name: Sprout Curation
galleries.note: Curator-run gallery known for research-led solo presentations and support of experimental younger practices.
